headline: Residents asked North Shore Music Theatre to provide ASL interpreters for its Christmas Carol show.
summary: Public speakers said the show runs December 3rd through December 23rd and needs two interpreters for at least 3 hours. Speakers estimated the cost at above 1,000 to a couple thousand dollars. Members said the commission cannot make the theater pay for interpreters. The commission also set two-year terms for officers and moved the officer election to January.
decisions: Tabled the election of chair and officers until January.
Approved two-year terms for all officers.
Approved adding the secretary position to the two-year terms.
discussion: ASL interpreters for Christmas Carol: Public speakers asked for two interpreters at the show so deaf and hard of hearing residents could attend, and said the theater had written that interpreters are a distraction. Members said the commission cannot force the theater to pay, and suggested residents contact the state or federal government.

Officer elections: Members discussed two-year terms, reinstating the vice-chair position, and the order of succession, with the chair, then vice-chair, then secretary. Members said a January vote would allow input from people who were not at the meeting.
Winter goals: Members reviewed winter goals for accessibility, including snow and ice clearing, accessible parking, and bus stops. Members said they met with MassDOT on winter planning.
Handicap parking enforcement: Members asked that Sergeant Nicholson and George Scarlatos be invited to a future meeting to explain how handicap parking violations are enforced.
